text:
rachel: Deploy to eu-central failed - multiple GPU pods stuck Pending, logs show sealedsecrets controller rejects because sops metadata references kms alias that doesn't exist in eu-central.
ops-bot: pipeline deploy/main finished: step `helmfile:sync` -> warnings + partial failures
rachel: I think this is a manifest order problem: Helm releases create namespaces via hooks after sealedsecrets are applied by gitops, so kube can't find namespace and sealedsecret creation is rejected.
tj: I saw `events` in controller: "namespace not found" then "decrypt error: kms key not found" in the same timeframe. Looks like two separate failure modes.
sam: TL;DR: two bugs converged: 1) gitops applied sealedsecrets before namespace creation (helmfile ordering), 2) sops metadata used `arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/xyz` which isn't aliased in eu-central.
marco: emergency mitigation I did: created the namespace first, then applied decrypted Secrets from CI runner using short-lived SSE key. Pods came up.
ci-bot: queued job infra/secret-canary-eu-central (decrypt+apply) scheduled
rachel: For immediate ops runbook I'm adding this one-liner to our playbook (run from a secure runner with credentials):
```
kubectl create ns ml-eu-central || true
sops -d secrets/ml/*.enc.yaml | kubectl apply -n ml-eu-central -f -
```
marco: not ideal long-term because we push plaintext through CI logs sometimes; prefer alternate approach.
tj: Long-term options discussion:
- multi-region KMS alias replication (pros: transparent for sops, cons: requires KMS replication, cost + admin)
- use a cross-region KMS alias in sops metadata pointing to an alias that we replicate (ops friction)
- pre-decrypt in a hardened CI step that writes k8s Secrets directly (pros: avoids KMS multi-region, cons: CI key management)
- enhance gitops ordering: ensure namespaces are created before sealedsecrets resources applied by using a `pre-sync` job or helm hook
rachel: Another mitigation: change sealed-secrets controller to run in `cluster` mode with an operator key per-region — expensive but fastest.
sam: We probably should add a Helm chart annotation so sealedsecret -> secret conversion triggers a rollout on the nodepool. Proposed annotation: `redwood.com/secrets-checksum: {{ include "app.configmap" . | sha256sum }}`
marco: Also adding a small pre-sync validation step in our pipeline that runs `kubectl get ns` + `kubectl get sealedsecret -o jsonpath=...` to detect likely mismatches before we push to clusters.
tj: Note on costs: KMS multi-region replication has per-key charges and cross-account considerations. Doing pre-decrypt in CI moves cost to ephemeral infra and increases audit surface.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0899 "sealedsecret KMS/ordering outage - eu-central" severity: medium
rachel: Action items: rachel->open RFC for pre-decrypt pattern and namespace pre-create ordering; tj->investigate KMS alias automation; sam->PR helm checksum annotation + gitops pre-sync check. I'll avoid broad rollouts to eu-central until canary passes.
marco: Saved logs and runbook to /ops/incidents/INC-2026-0899, adding exact `kubectl` commands.
sam: FYI I put a canary that recreates 3 sealedsecrets via the new pre-decrypt job in eu-central; monitoring GPU pool now.
ci-bot: job infra/secret-canary-eu-central completed: success (3/3)
rachel: Good, re-enable gradual rollouts but keep monitoring for 4 hours. I'll update this thread with any regressions.
